modules.title: Module 2: Multi-Table Queries & Relational JOINs
modules.description: Connect related data across multiple tables using primary keys and foreign keys.

topics.title: SQL Lesson 6: Multi-table queries with JOINs
topics.description: Combine information from the Movies and Boxoffice tables with INNER JOIN.

sqlExercise.schemaSql:
CREATE TABLE movies (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  title TEXT,
  director TEXT,
  year INTEGER,
  length_minutes INTEGER
);


CREATE TABLE boxoffice (
  movie_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  rating REAL,
  domestic_sales INTEGER,
  international_sales INTEGER,
  FOREIGN KEY (movie_id) REFERENCES movies(id)
);
sqlExercise.defaultQuery: SELECT * FROM movies INNER JOIN boxoffice ON movies.id = boxoffice.movie_id;

tasks.instruction: Find the domestic and international sales for each movie.
tasks.expectedQuery: SELECT title, domestic_sales, international_sales FROM movies JOIN boxoffice ON movies.id = boxoffice.movie_id;
tasks.solution: SELECT title, domestic_sales, international_sales FROM movies JOIN boxoffice ON movies.id = boxoffice.movie_id;

tasks.instruction: Show the sales numbers for each movie that did better internationally rather than domestically.
tasks.expectedQuery: SELECT title, domestic_sales, international_sales FROM movies JOIN boxoffice ON movies.id = boxoffice.movie_id WHERE international_sales > domestic_sales;
tasks.solution: SELECT title, domestic_sales, international_sales FROM movies JOIN boxoffice ON movies.id = boxoffice.movie_id WHERE international_sales > domestic_sales;

tasks.instruction: List all the movies by their ratings in descending order.
tasks.expectedQuery: SELECT title, rating FROM movies JOIN boxoffice ON movies.id = boxoffice.movie_id ORDER BY rating DESC;
tasks.solution: SELECT title, rating FROM movies JOIN boxoffice ON movies.id = boxoffice.movie_id ORDER BY rating DESC;
